review.summary: Independent read of the four supplied files confirms F1's core structural claim: no tracker adapter seam exists in the snapshot. Source is a closed two-branch union of beads-native shapes; loadIssues spawns the bd binary inline; types.ts frames the domain model as a reduction of bd export; IssueStore holds exactly one Source and emits a single hardcoded status row ("source-1"/"Configured tracker"). These are read-only structural facts. However, F1 overstates two consequences: Dependency.type is plain string, so non-beads trackers need not fake beads vocabulary or widen types; and the last-hyphen split for projectOf assumes an identifier contract absent here, making cross-repository collision an unproven behavioral claim without omitted composition code. The type-level attribution gap is verifiable: Issue lacks source/repo fields, so merged issues from distinct adapters would be indistinguishable. Linear remains correctly documented as optional roadmap work. I split the difference: support the adapter-absence claim as directly observable, but mark needs_test for the unproven multi-repository collision and project-split correctness claims that require omitted application logic to demonstrate.

votes.reason: The adapter seam absence is structurally verifiable: Source is a closed union of beads-native shapes, loadIssues execs bd inline, types.ts documents the model as bd export reduction, and IssueStore carries one Source with hardcoded status literals. I support this leg. However, F1 bundles unproven behavioral claims: (1) that last-hyphen splitting is incorrect requires an id format contract not in the snapshot; (2) that identical prefixes across workspaces cause merging requires omitted grouping/composition code to demonstrate; (3) that Dependency.type forces beads vocabulary is overstated since it is plain string. The attribution gap (no source/repo on Issue) is type-level real but its consequences need the omitted application layer. Priority 3 design debt is appropriate. Verdict is needs_test because the improvement criteria require behavioral verification (items 3-5) that cannot be validated from this selection alone.
